Grafton.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Grafton calls follow the ground the town sits on: tygart Valley River (through the city), Tygart Lake east of town, wooded hillsides rising around the historic neighborhoods. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, striped skunks in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

Spring is denning season here, summer is bat season in the older housing stock, and fall brings a second push as squirrels and rodents look for winter shelter. Grafton layers Victorian and rail-era homes and brick blocks in the river valley, the town where Mother's Day began. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.

faqs.q: How much will it cost to get wildlife out of my Flemington home?
faqs.a: It depends on the job — a single squirrel entry sealed early is very different work from a raccoon family in a chimney or a bat colony in the attic. We inspect first and provide a straightforward quote after inspection, so you know the full scope before any work starts.

faqs.q: What is digging under Flemington porches and sheds?
faqs.a: Striped skunks under the porches and woodchucks at the shed and garden edges — both routine in creek-bottom soil. We identify the den first, remove the animal as a licensed WDCA, and screen the opening.
